songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Early blues set with standout Heads Up, Midnight Hour, raw R&B
ai_show_review.blurb: The March 19 1966 Pico Acid Test captures a brief early‑Dead blues set. Highlights include Jerry’s blistering guitar on “Heads Up” and “Midnight Hour,” plus the soulful “You See a Broken Heart.” The soundboard source is clean with good stereo separation, though the mix leans heavy on guitar.
ai_show_review.review: On March 19, 1966 the Grateful Dead took the stage at Carthay Studios for the historic Pico Acid Test. This was an early‑period gig that leans heavily into raw R&B and blues, offering a concise set that feels more like a snapshot of the band’s formative sound than a polished concert. Jerry Garcia dominates the mix with scorching blues licks on “Heads Up,” the “Stormy Monday Jam,” and “Midnight Hour,” delivering the kind of guitar work that makes this tape a favorite for those interested in his early style. Bob Weir’s vocals are a little out of key at times, but his presence adds to the gritty authenticity of the performance. The soundboard recording is praised for its clarity, excellent stereo separation and forward‑projected guitars, even if some reviewers suggest a mono mix might tame the Jerry‑heavy balance. While improvisation is limited compared to later shows, the set’s historical value—capturing the Dead in their teenage blues phase—is undeniable.

best_recording.reason: Clean soundboard with excellent stereo separation; captures the full early blues set and highlights Jerry’s guitar work despite a slightly guitar‑heavy mix.

key_highlights: Standout early‑Dead blues numbers like “Heads Up” and “Midnight Hour”.
